report.stage_table: from clocks: setup (lookup+zero), word-table prefix, decode+add, radix select+gather, bitonic sort, candidate write (theta atomicMax, cut read, write), threadfence, done ticket, merge select, merge scatter; mean per block (mean over warps, then blocks and slices) and critical path (median over slices of the slowest pre-merge block's slowest warp per stage); merge tail (globaltimer: merging block end - latest candidate-write end). Clock-build values; the radix, gather, bitonic and theta barriers have no clock sites, so their waits are inside those stage times
report.barrier_table: clocks: the seven instrumented sites (S1-S7), mean wait per warp, critical-path wait, share of barrier time. ncu: every BAR instruction by source line (all sites, including radix passes, gather, bitonic and theta), barrier-stall samples and share
report.resources: ncu launch statistics: registers per thread, static and dynamic shared memory per block, driver shared memory, occupancy limits and blocks per SM (minimum limit), waves per SM; ptxas -v as a cross-check
report.coalescing: ncu source counters (-lineinfo): decode loop encoded-word loads (rbp_extract, range_bitpack.h) and impacts loads: requests (warp instructions), L2 theoretical sectors, sectors per request against ideal
report.radix_contention: ncu: samples and stall reasons on the bucket atomicAdd line (mio throttle = shared-memory instruction queue throttle, short scoreboard, etc.); CPU replay: per range the share of documents with score 0, keys counted in each pass, the share of ranges whose first-pass largest bucket holds more than half the keys counted, and the modeled same-bucket depth per warp atomic instruction (32 consecutive slots per warp)
report.decode_stalls: ncu: stall reasons on the encoded-load line and the impacts-load + score-atomicAdd line (all SASS of the line, so the consumers of the loads that carry long-scoreboard stalls are included), and on the load instructions themselves
report.host_vs_gpu: nsys per query: launch API, launch to kernel start, kernel, D2H copy, kernel end to D2H start, kernel end to copy return (GPU end to result back on the host), copy return after D2H end; unprofiled wall and GPU share from the reference step

reading_rules_registered_before_data.a_unrolled_decode: supported if decode+add is at least 25% of the pre-merge critical path at some k AND long-scoreboard stalls are at least 50% of the samples on the encoded-load line AND DRAM throughput is below 50% of peak (latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound)
reading_rules_registered_before_data.b_radix_contention: supported if radix select+gather is at least 20% of the pre-merge critical path at some k AND the bucket atomicAdd line holds at least 5% of kernel samples AND the replay's mean same-bucket depth per warp atomic instruction is at least 8
reading_rules_registered_before_data.c_result_buffer: supported if the median kernel end to copy return is at least 5% of the median unprofiled wall per query at some k
reading_rules_registered_before_data.note: rules decide what the profile supports, not what is written; the owner decides which changes to implement

gpu_policy.idle_check: before every GPU process (code/session_lib.sh wait_idle): no compute process on the GPU (nvidia-smi), none of our GPU jobs (scorer, nsys, ncu), and no other 'run_*' script outside this session (pgrep -f '[r]un_'); otherwise wait in 30 s steps up to IDLE_WAIT_MAX = 14400 s, then the session stops

amendments.text: Overlap classification fix before Measurement E session 3. In session 2 the fixtures step (one Python process that runs ~216 short scorer subprocesses) was flagged as overlapping in every attempt: most of its own subprocesses exit before the 0.5 s poll can read their owner, so they were logged as 'gone' and, in pmon, as unknown PIDs, both counted as other users' processes (attempt 1: 32 flagged PIDs, 31 pmon-only with 0 MiB, 1 with 154 MiB; attempt 0 also had one genuine other process, 920 MiB at 99% SM). Fix (code/session_lib.sh, code/overlap.py): a process whose owner cannot be read is classified as ours ('oursname') only if nvidia-smi's process path is one of our build directories' scorer binaries ((^|/)build/<dir>/<label>/scorer); a pmon row is ours if its process name is exactly 'scorer' (the command column is logged as 'ours' or '-', never the name). Everything else is unchanged: another user's process still counts as an overlap. Session 2 (gate ctrl-02, fixtures overlap-1..3 preserved) was stopped by hand at 17:50:16Z and is recorded as failed; session 3 relaunches the same plan from the fixed commit (rebuilt; SASS must equal the recorded hashes).

Measurement E gates run contended (CONTENDED=1 in code/session_lib.sh): they are correctness checks only, so they do not wait for other users' GPU processes and overlapped steps are not replaced; every overlap is still recorded per process (logs/overlap-checks.jsonl). Our own GPU jobs are still never run concurrently. The timing run is unchanged (idle check before every process, 300 s retries, overlapped processes preserved and rerun). Session 3 was stopped by hand at 18:10:52Z after gate ctrl-03 passed (under the full idle rule) and gate v3-3-01 had paused for an idle check; session 4 rebuilds at the amendment commit, gates the six v3 builds contended (v3-3 as -02), keeps ctrl-03 (ctrl is always built from 74dd5d3; SASS 53eb3cac16e4bc19), then times.

E1 reading for Measurement E (decided after the run): E1 is applied per W, at W=4096. Reasons: W=4096 with 256 threads was chosen as the configuration before Measurement E (Step 1's prompt of this experiment, 'The chosen configuration is W=4096 with 256 threads', and the owner's 2026-11-21 decision), and E1 compares each variant against v3-3 at the same W. The registered clause 'it must pass at every W it was timed at' (written by Claude when registering) is replaced by this reading. Outcome: at W=4096 unroll2, unroll4, D, u2m and u4m all pass E1; E2 picks unroll4 (geometric mean 0.904 vs 0.942); E3 picks u4m (passes E1 and beats D: six-cell geometric mean 0.553 vs D 0.609; u4m/D at W=4096 0.823 [0.799, 0.842], 0.846 [0.842, 0.851], 0.903 [0.897, 0.909] at k=10/100/1000). Final variant: u4m (A with U=4 + D) at W=4096. Not adopted: v3-3 at W=1024 is the fastest k=10 cell (0.0907 ms vs u4m at W=4096 0.0987 ms), but using it would need a second index and a second code path; D loses at W=1024, k=10 (1.134 [1.126, 1.141] x v3-3). The run's analysis output (paired-statistics.json, tables.md) is left as produced under the registered clause; both readings are reported.

decision_rules.E1: a variant is adopted if its ratio to v3-3 (same W) has an upper 95% bound < 1 at some k and no k's lower bound is > 1.02; evaluated at each W the variant is timed at, and it must pass at every such W (unroll2/unroll4: W=4096 only)
decision_rules.E2: unroll: U=2 vs U=4, the lower geometric mean across k of the ratio-to-v3-3 point estimates (W=4096) among those passing E1; none if neither passes
decision_rules.E3: final variant = u2m or u4m if it passes E1 and its geometric mean of point estimates over the six (W, k) cells is lower than D's (the lower of the two if both qualify); otherwise D if D passes E1; otherwise v3-3 (nothing adopted)
decision_rules.E4: for the final variant, per k: recommend W=1024 only if W=1024 / W=4096 (same session, paired) has an upper 95% bound < 1; otherwise W=4096; also report whether one W is best for all k. Label: calibration tuning, to be frozen before held-out evaluation
decision_rules.E1_as_amended: applied per W at W=4096 (the configuration chosen before Measurement E); see amendments

measurement_E.report: per k: variant | W | pooled median ms | ratio to v3-3 [95%] | ratio to ctrl W=1024 [95%]; E1-E4 outcomes; final variant and W choice

gpu_policy.idle_check: before every GPU process: no compute process, none of our GPU jobs, no other run_* script outside the session; when busy, retry every 300 s (IDLE_POLL=300) until a deadline 6 h after the session launch (IDLE_DEADLINE), then the session stops and the owner is told
gpu_policy.overlap: a process that overlaps another user's GPU process is preserved as <tag>-overlap-<n> and rerun (at most 3 replacements per slot, then the session stops)
